Submitted answer: True (the expression is always an integer).

Verified: the identity ∏_{n≥1} cos(x/2^n) = sin x / x with x = π/k gives π · (k sin(π/k)/π) / sin(π/k) = k. So the expression equals k, an integer, whenever it is defined.

The expression is undefined for k = 0 and k = ±1, where the denominator vanishes or π/k does not exist. A strict reading of "any integer k" could therefore be argued to make the claim false. The question asks whether the expression is an integer, and wherever it has a value that value is exactly k. For k = ±1 the expression tends to ±1 in the limit. I judge the intended answer to be "yes, it equals k", which matches the submitted "True".
